title: Samsung semiconductor employees leak confidential data to ChatGPT
description: After Samsung's semiconductor division lifted an internal ban and allowed employees to use ChatGPT from March 2023, engineers pasted confidential source code, chip-defect-detection code, and internal meeting notes into the chatbot on at least three separate occasions within about three weeks. Because such inputs could be retained or exposed by the third-party service, Samsung subsequently banned employee use of ChatGPT and other generative AI tools on company devices and networks, announced around 1-2 May 2023.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty. Exact dates of the three individual leak incidents are drawn from secondary English-language reporting on original Korean-language coverage and are approximate.

root_cause: Absence of technical controls (e.g. data-loss-prevention tooling) or clear employee guidance after the internal ChatGPT ban was lifted, combined with employees' lack of awareness that data submitted to a third-party generative AI service could be retained on external servers.

citations.title: Samsung Bans ChatGPT, Google Bard, Other Generative AI Use by Staff After Leak

relationships.reason: A documented, technically-enforced acceptable-use policy for third-party generative AI tools directly addresses this leak.
This is a canonical example of the enterprise data-exposure risk this board question is designed to surface.
